MINUTES
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MARCH 27, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:02 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Shinn, Silvano, Griggs, Robinson, Medawar,
  Ciarolla, and Schachter
  Committee Members Absent:  Harik, Martin and Nilsen
  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 27, 2023
  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 27, 2023, EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.
4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
  NONE.
5.  STAFF ITEMS
A.  REVIEW OF PERMIT REQUIREMENT FOR GUIDES OF TRAIL RIDING
  OPERATORS
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written
  report.
  Supervisor Pinuelas clarified that guides would still be required to be covered by the
  trail riding operator’s insurance but under the revision, there would no longer be a
  requirement that at least one guide have a trainer’s permit and pay associated fee, in
  response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.
  MEMBER SHINN asked if the names and contact information for the guides could be
  collected along with signatures confirming they are aware of the rules and conditions.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 27, 2023
  1
   Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed, adding that a section could be added for the guide
  information and signatures.
  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN to:
  APPROVE THE CONDITIONS BE MODIFIED SO THAT GUIDES ARE
  COVERED UNDER AN OPERATOR’S HORSE TRAINER PERMIT AND NOT
  REQUIRED TO OBTAIN INDIVIDUAL PERMITS.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.
B.  EQUESTRIAN FEES REVIEW
  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.
  Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed that the Ernie Howlett Park Equestrian Center fee
  increases of three percent are for the 2023-2024 fiscal year in response to CHAIR
  SCHACHTER. Supervisor Pinuelas noted that when the fees are brought to the
  Committee for review next year, assuming no significant changes, they would be for
  year three with an increase of three percent with two percent increases annually
  thereafter.
  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER GRIGGS, TO APPROVE AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE TO:
  APPROVE THE EQUESTRIAN FEES AS PROPOSED AND RECOMMEND
  REVIEW BY THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION FOR FY 2023-24
  OR CALENDAR YEAR 2024 (FOR HORSE TRAINERS BUSINESS LICENSE
  TAX RENEWALS AND PUBLIC ARENA USE PERMIT FEES).
  AYES: Brtis, Shinn, Silvano, Griggs, Robinson, Medawar, Ciarolla, and Schachter
  ABSENT: Harik, Martin and Nilsen

C.  ARENA #3 AND #4 RENOVATION SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)
  Supervisor Pinuelas shared that the Portuguese Bend Horse Show (PBHS) did not
  have a representative for the subcommittee, therefore, Staff recommended the
  assessment of Arenas #3 and #4 be tabled and revisited after this year’s show.
  Supervisor Pinuelas clarified that plans for renovation of Arena #2 are still moving
  forward in response to MEMBER SHINN.
  Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed that the item could be added to a future agenda list in
  response to MEMBER SHINN.
  MEMBER GRIGGS asked if the subcommittee could meet in September after the
  horse show. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that she could check in with the organizers
  after the show to determine their status at that point.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 27, 2023
  2
   CHAIR SCHACHTER stated PBHS are not committing to the project at this time and
  noted how the PCHA medal finals are assigned.
  MEMBER SILVANO stated that the finals are not awarded by bidding in response to
  MEMBER GRIGGS. MEMBER SILVANO stated that she believed the medal finals
  are granted to organizations on a biannual basis in response to CHAIR
  SCHACHTER.
  Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed that PBHS are still partnering with the City on the
  funding of the Arena 2 renovation in response to MEMBER SILVANO. CHAIR
  SCHACHTER also affirmed noting there is no commitment right now for Arenas 3
  and 4. Supervisor Pinuelas noted that when PBHS initially approached Staff
  regarding the Arena 3 and 4 renovations, PBHS noted that it was a wish list item
  and not a dire need. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted the cost was
  fully determined and is likely higher than early estimates.
D.  HORSE TRAINER LICENSE AND PERMIT UPDATE

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that he has not seen Raquel Santos training in
  City facilities and that it is unknown if she is training in the area in response to CHAIR
  SCHACHTER. Supervisor Pinuelas noted that Staff has a call to confirm.
  Supervisor Pinuelas explained that category one trainers are those that operate at
  private facilities meaning they do not use the City’s public horse arenas or the trail
  system or operate in City parks in response to MEMBER GRIGGS. Supervisor
  Pinuelas responded that the owner of Seahorse was accidentally left off the list but
  has a current license in addition to Devon Gibson who trains at Seahorse in response
  to MEMBER GRIGGS.
  MEMBER SILVANO stated that a license is required to do business in the City in
  response to MEMBER GRIGGS.
  MEMBER SHINN asked if Devon Gibson could train in the public arenas with a
  category one license. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that is not allowed with a
  category one license.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if the Committee had interest in adding and revisiting
  the issue of horse veterinarians and horse shoers licensing by adding the item to a
  future agenda. Discussion ensued and CHAIR SCHACHTER directed Staff to return
  with the item to a future meeting agenda.
E.  AMBASSADOR PROGRAM UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update stating that when Staff last met with the
  Subcommittee which includes Members Robinson and Harik, they discussed initial
  ideas for the program. She stated that Staff is working to gather information from the
  Sheriff’s Posse and will be reaching out the Palos Verdes Peninsula Horseman’s

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 27, 2023
  3
   Association to assess any resources available to support the program. She added
  that Staff is also looking to risk management to see what would be needed to set up
  this type of volunteer program.

F.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  MEMBER ROBINSON stated there the bees are back at the top of the trail at Spinning
  Wheel. Superintendent Goldsmith stated he would inspect the area.

G.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief update and noted the event would take place on
  Saturday, May 13 with the ride starting at 9:00 am. She stated the Scouts would be
  returning to host their traditional pancake breakfast to the excitement of many. She
  added that marketing would begin in the coming weeks.

H.  EQUESTRIAN RECOGNITION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas shared that $175 had been collected to date with a goal of
  approximately $450. She added that donations would continue to be collected
  through April 11. Supervisor Pinuelas noted that PVPHA had shared the information
  regarding the project via their newsletter to assist in soliciting donations.

  MEMBER SILVANO asked for more information stating she would be securing an
  additional donation. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that she would reach out to her
  with details.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that Superintendent Goldsmith was aware of issues on
  her trail and that it looked great that day.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER noted the growth of the weeds as a result of the rain.

B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed that the Public Service Video idea to assist with horse
  safety awareness could be revisited in response to MEMBER ROBINSON. MEMBER
  ROBINSON stated the videos could explain how to conduct oneself on the trails and
  how to safely approach when coming up behind a horse noting an issue with an
  unleashed dog on a trail.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that it could serve as a parallel to the Ambassador
  Program.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 27, 2023
  4
   MEMBER MEDAWAR stated that as a Reserve for the Palos Verdes Estates Police
  Department when monitoring the trails, he provides education to dog walkers
  because the biggest issue they encounter is unleashed dogs. He stated he does not
  think Lomita Station has the resources to do that.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER noted a request from the Sheriffs for vehicles that can be used
  on the trails. She added there was eagerness for the Ambassador Program to assist
  with trail issues.

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated she heard there is an issue with E-bikes on the Dapplegray
  side of the hill.

  MEMBER SILVANO asked about the rules regarding the number of allowed
  absences from Committee meetings. CHAIR SCHACHTER noted that is up to the
  City Council. CHAIR SCHACHTER added that the Council would be looking at each
  Committee and the number of members on the Committees.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated the City Celebration would be held on Saturday,
  September 23 in response to MEMBER SHINN.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHACHTER ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:42 pm.
  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Pam Brown Schachter, Chair
  Community Services Supervisor

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
